title: KCP hello request (DESIGN.md §11.1, §11.6.1 pre-auth family)
description: Read: never mutates authoritative or user-visible state and never carries meta (closed shape — a read carrying meta, hence an idempotency key, fails; §11.2, R0 KENV-01). Pre-auth negotiation operation: the closed shape carries no realm_id, project_id, identity, or credential member (§11.1; gap note KG1). Begins every connection-oriented binding; the server selects the highest mutually supported version or returns unsupported-version (§11.1). kcp-hello.schema.json pins the same §11.1 shapes standalone; this schema is their command framing (gap note KG1). Registry (core_v1): surface external_client / pre-auth channel (assurance: none). Surface and actor kind are registry-enforced, not schema-expressible (gap note KG14 for dual-surface ops).

supported_versions.description: Client-supported protocol versions; at most 256 list items per request (§11.8).

requested_features.description: Feature bundles the client wants; may be empty. A feature must be negotiated before use (§11.9).

args.description: The §11.1 HelloRequest field list verbatim, carried as command args (gap note KG1). Authentication occurs in the transport, never as an identity claim here (§11.1).

displayName.description: Display name bounded by the §11.8 cap of 256 Unicode scalar values, length-bounded again at admission.

ext.description: Extensions keyed by a reverse-domain namespace (§11.9); never interpreted as identity, authorization, budget, or policy.

featureId.description: Feature-bundle name from the §11.6 table (e.g. core_v1). Bundles are atomic: implement every operation/schema/conformance case in a listed bundle or do not advertise it.

identifier.description: Opaque identifier, at most 128 bytes (§11.8); visible-ASCII alphabet is a K0 extraction decision (spec/schemas/README.md).

protocolVersion.description: Negotiated KCP major.minor version; the initial protocol version is "0.1" (§11).
